item.text:
**Verdict:** mixed, leaning negative. I found solid evidence that Turkey’s health procurement and some core state institutions were run in a technocratic, rules-based way in 2024. But the broader social-service picture still looks politically selective, with strong evidence of discrimination against Kurds, women, LGBT people, and refugees, plus local governance disruptions that likely weakened service delivery.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Great Savings in Public Medical Supplies and Pharmaceuticals Procurement | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-10-17 | [link](https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Eng/Home/EngIcerik/3998) | DMO says its Healthcare Products Market scaled to 10,000 medical supplies and 3,000 pharmaceuticals, covering 62% of medical supplies and 93% of pharmaceuticals for the Health Ministry and university hospitals with competitive pricing, quality, and rapid supply. This is strong evidence of competent, professional social-service procurement. | 6B.4; also 6B.2 |
| Positive | Foreword by Director General | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-05-03 | [link](https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Eng/Home/EngIcerik/1212) | DMO describes itself as a central purchasing body using a “professional and innovative approach,” emphasizing transparency, competition, accountability, and fast, comprehensive service. It also says the Healthcare Products Market digitalized hospital drug and medical-supply procurement. | 6B.4; also 6B.2 |
| Positive | 1.1 Governing Bodies - TCMB 2024 Annual Report | Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye | 2024 | [link](https://www3.tcmb.gov.tr/yillikrapor/2024/en/m-1-1/) | The CBRT board and MPC were staffed by named economists and academics, with formal terms, meetings, and recorded resolutions. This is indirect but useful evidence that Erdoğan still relied on professional technocrats in at least one major public institution rather than pure patronage. | 6B.4; also 5B.7, 5B.9 |
| Positive | Türkiye - Socially Inclusive Green Transition Project | World Bank | 2024-03-06 | [link](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099031124170520652) | The project aimed to improve women and youth economic opportunities, support women- and youth-led MSMEs, and fund local infrastructure in less developed areas. This is not direct state social-service management, but it is evidence of professionally designed, vulnerable-group-oriented public support. | 6B.4; also 6B.2, 6B.3 |
| Positive | World Bank to Support Women, Youth Owned Small Businesses and Industry Adapt to Green Transition in Türkiye | World Bank | 2024-04-01 | [link](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/03/29/world-bank-to-support-women-youth-owned-small-businesses-and-industry-adapt-to-green-transition-in-turkiye) | The World Bank said the package was meant to be equitable and inclusive for women, youth, and vulnerable groups in less developed areas, with access to finance and local infrastructure. That supports a technocratic, programmatic welfare model, though it is indirect evidence of Erdoğan’s own governing style. | 6B.4; also 6B.2, 6B.3 |
| Negative | Turkey: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [link](https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House says AKP politics favored Sunni Muslims, Kurdish parties faced harassment, women and LGBT people remained politically marginalized, and refugees faced restrictions and anti-foreigner rhetoric. That points to politically selective state treatment rather than neutral, professional social-service delivery. | 6B.4; also 6B.1, 6B.3 |
| Negative | World Report 2024: Türkiye | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | [link](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/turkey) | HRW says women and girls lacked effective protection from domestic violence, anti-LGBT hate speech was central to the campaign, and refugees and migrants faced coercive treatment. This is strong evidence that vulnerable-group welfare was not being managed in an even-handed, professional way. | 6B.4; also 6B.2, 6B.3 |
| Negative | Shock, confusion as Turkey seizes earthquake survivors' homes | Reuters | 2024-03-18 | [link](https://www.reuters.com/commodities/shock-confusion-as-turkey-seizes-earthquake-survivors-homes-2024-03-18/) | Reuters reported deed transfers in Hatay to the Treasury under an urban-planning amendment, alarming survivors. In a disaster-hit region, that is a major sign of weak or politically driven administration rather than careful professional service management. | 6B.4; also 6B.2, 6B.3, 5B.9 |
| Negative | Turkey to lift minimum retirement pay, impose minimum corporate tax | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-07-16 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/turkey-to-lift-minimum-retirement-pay-impose-minimum-corporate-tax/2176793/) | Reuters framed the minimum-pension increase as targeted relief in an inflationary environment. It helps some elderly people, but the narrowness looks more like political damage control than a professionally managed social-protection expansion. | 6B.4; also 6B.2, 6B.3, 5B.7 |

Search gap: I found direct evidence for professional health procurement and broader technocratic capacity, but very little direct 2024 evidence on education, disability services, child protection, or the staffing of the relevant ministries. The best positive evidence is concentrated in procurement and digitally managed health purchasing, while the strongest negatives come from discrimination, politicized local control, and housing/security shocks in disaster areas.
